funFacts.text: Their upperparts and wings are rufous-brown and their rump, uppertail coverts, and tail are more rufescent.
The ruby-crowned tanager feeds on arthropods, fruit, and seeds; fruits include both wild and cultivated species.
Its nest is a cup made from grass with a lining of rootlets and is typically in dense vegetation within about 2 m (7 ft) of the ground.
The ruby-crowned tanager's song is described as a "simple high chirping tjur wdit tjur- -" and its call a "high, bouncing trit-trit trit- -".

summary: The ruby-crowned tanager (Tachyphonus coronatus) is a species of bird in the family Thraupidae, the tanagers and allies. It is found in Argentina, Brazil, Paraguay, and as a vagrant to Uruguay.

The ruby-crowned tanager was formally described in 1822 with the binomial Agelaius Coronatus [sic], mistakenly classifying it as a New World blackbird. It now shares the genus Tachyphonus with four other species and is sister to the white-lined tanager (T. rufus).
